answers: I'm up against a deadline.
I'm racing against the clock.
questions.hint: up against = ~에 직면한, race against the clock = 시간과 싸우다

questions.korean: 그 소식은 너무 좋아서 믿기 힘들어.
answers: The news is too good to be true.
It sounds too good to be true.
questions.hint: too good to be true = 믿기 어려울 정도로 좋은

answers: I'm just browsing.
I'm just looking around.
She always looks on the bright side.
She always sees the glass as half full.
questions.hint: look on the bright side = 밝은 면을 보다
questions.explanation: see the glass as half full = 낙관적으로 보다

answers: He has a short temper.
He loses his temper easily.
I think that he will come.
I believe he'll show up.
I don't know whether she is married.
I'm not sure if she's married.
I doubt whether he is telling the truth.
I question if he's being honest.

questions.korean: 중요한 건 우리가 최선을 다했다는 거야.
answers: What matters is that we did our best.
The important thing is that we tried our hardest.
questions.hint: What matters is that ~ / The important thing is that ~

questions.korean: 그가 제시간에 올지 안 올지가 문제야.
answers: The question is whether he will come on time.
It's a question of whether he'll be on time.
I was late for the meeting due to traffic.
I missed the meeting because of a traffic jam.
questions.explanation: due to = because of (명사 앞에 사용)

answers: As a result, they won the contract.
Consequently, they secured the deal.

questions.korean: 그 폭풍으로 인해 많은 나무가 쓰러졌어.
answers: The storm caused many trees to fall.
Many trees fell due to the storm.
Thanks to you, my work became much easier.
Because of your help, things got a lot easier.
questions.explanation: thanks to = 긍정적 원인, because of = 중립적 원인

questions.korean: 그 사고의 결과로, 그는 두 달을 쉬어야 했어.
answers: As a result of the accident, he had to rest for two months.
The accident resulted in him resting for two months.
questions.hint: as a result of + 명사 = ~의 결과로

answers: Although I was tired, I ran to the end.
Even though I was exhausted, I finished the race.
Despite the rain, they continued the game.
In spite of the rain, they kept playing.
questions.explanation: despite/in spite of 뒤엔 명사 또는 ~ing

questions.korean: 열심히 했지만, 그녀는 시험을 통과하지 못했어.
answers: She tried hard, yet she couldn't pass the exam.
Even though she worked hard, she failed the test.
Despite having no money, he was happy.
Even though he had no money, he was happy.
Despite practicing for a long time, he is still clumsy.
Even though he's been practicing for years, he's still not good.
He must be at home now.
He has to be home right now.

questions.korean: 그녀는 의사임에 틀림없어. 하얀 가운을 입고 있잖아.
answers: She must be a doctor. She's wearing a white coat.
She has to be a doctor — she's in a white coat.

questions.korean: 그가 벌써 집에 갔을 리가 없어.
answers: He can't have gone home already.
There's no way he's already left.
questions.hint: can't be / can't have p.p. = ~일 리가 없다

questions.korean: 그녀는 피곤할 것 같아. 오늘 일을 많이 했으니까.
answers: She might be tired. She worked a lot today.
She's probably tired since she worked so hard today.

questions.korean: 그 패키지가 이미 도착했을 수도 있어.
answers: The package might have already arrived.
The package could have been delivered by now.
Would you mind waiting for a moment?
Could you please wait for a second?
questions.hint: Would you mind + ~ing? / Could you please ~?

answers: May I ask for your advice?
Could I get your input on something?
questions.explanation: May I = 매우 격식체, Could I = 일반 공손체

answers: I'll look into it.
Allow me to check on that.

questions.korean: 그 점에 대해 더 말씀해 주실 수 있으세요?
answers: Could you elaborate on that point?
Would you mind explaining that in more detail?
questions.hint: elaborate on = ~에 대해 더 자세히 설명하다

answers: Is this seat taken?
Do you mind if I sit here?
questions.hint: Is this seat taken? = 이 자리에 사람 있어요?
questions.explanation: Is this taken? = 가장 자연스러운 표현

questions.korean: 내가 사랑하는 건 바로 그 음악이야.
answers: It is the music that I love.
It's the music that I'm really into.
questions.explanation: 강조 구문: 강조하고 싶은 부분을 It is ~ that 사이에 넣음

questions.korean: 그를 행복하게 만든 건 바로 그 편지였어.
answers: It was the letter that made him happy.
It was that letter that brought him joy.

questions.korean: 내가 그녀를 만난 건 바로 이 도시에서야.
answers: It was in this city that I met her.
It was here in this city that I first met her.

questions.korean: 그가 원하는 건 그냥 쉬는 거야.
answers: What he wants is just to rest.
All he wants is just to relax.
questions.hint: What + 주어 + want is + to 부정사

answers: That's exactly what I'm worried about.
That is precisely what concerns me.
Please find the attached file.
Please see the attachment.
questions.hint: Please find the attached = 첨부 파일 안내 이메일 표현

answers: I apologize for the late reply.
Sorry for getting back to you so late.
Please let me know if you have any further questions.
Feel free to reach out if you need anything else.
questions.hint: Please let me know if + 조건절

answers: Could we schedule a meeting?
Would it be possible to set up a meeting?
questions.hint: Could we schedule / Would it be possible to ~?

answers: I will look into this matter.
I'll review this and get back to you.
I'm not sure if I can make it on time.
I don't know whether I'll be there in time.
questions.hint: make it on time = 제시간에 도착하다/해내다
questions.explanation: in time = 제때에, on time = 정시에

answers: The event was canceled two weeks ahead of time.
The event was called off two weeks in advance.
questions.hint: ahead of time = in advance = 미리, 사전에

questions.korean: 나는 항상 마감 직전에 일을 해.
answers: I always work at the last minute.
I always leave things until the last moment.
questions.hint: at the last minute = 마감 직전에

answers: He manages his time efficiently.
He is very good at time management.
It has been ten years since we met.
Ten years have passed since we first met.

questions.korean: 그가 왜 사직했는지 정확히 알 수 없지만, 아마 더 좋은 기회가 생겼을 거야.
answers: I'm not sure exactly why he resigned, but he might have found a better opportunity.
I don't know why he quit, but he probably got a better offer.

questions.korean: 내가 더 어렸을 때 더 많은 것들을 시도했더라면 좋았을 텐데.
answers: I wish I had tried more things when I was younger.
If only I had taken more chances in my youth.

questions.korean: 그것 때문에 회의가 취소됐고, 결과적으로 우리는 계획을 다시 짜야 했어.
answers: That caused the meeting to be canceled, and as a result, we had to redo our plans.
Because of that, the meeting was called off, so we had to start from scratch.
questions.hint: cause ~ to be canceled + as a result
questions.explanation: start from scratch = 처음부터 다시 시작하다

answers: Despite that, he did his best.
In spite of everything, he gave it his all.
questions.explanation: give it one's all = 최선을 다하다

questions.korean: 내가 강조하고 싶은 건, 팀워크야말로 성공의 열쇠라는 거야.
answers: What I want to emphasize is that teamwork is the key to success.
The point I'm making is that teamwork is what makes us succeed.
questions.hint: What I want to emphasize is that ~
